speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me exactly what happens when you wake up frightened, and does anyone else in the house seem to be having similar issues at night? Also, have you noticed any changes in your breathing or leg movements recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Have you noticed any involuntary movements of your legs or arms, especially just before these frightening episodes? Additionally, have you had any recent falls or injuries, and do your parents see any twitching or jerking during her sleep?

REQUEST TEST: Sleep_Study; REQUEST IMAGES: EEG

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since your sleep study and EEG are normal, we can rule out seizures or sleep apnea. Do you or your parents ever see you acting out your dreams, like kicking or punching, while you appear to be asleep? Also, have you been under any recent stress, such as starting a new school or having a scary event at home?

REQUEST TEST: ACTGRAPH; REQUEST IMAGES: Video_Polysomnography

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the Actiwatch and video review are normal and rule out parasomnias, have you noticed if these frightening episodes happen specifically around the time she usually falls asleep or right before waking up in the morning? Also, do you feel any sudden, intense pressure or pain in your chest or stomach during these events?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Difficulty sleeping with episodes of waking up frightened. I also have Yelling and crying during sleep episodes, Temporary post-episode tiredness, Recollection of bad dreams, Bedtime procrastination.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Nightmare Disorder. Based on your description of waking fully alert, terrified, and having recall of the bad dreams, this fits the classic presentation of nightmares rather than sleep terrors, which you would not remember. We will focus on addressing the bedtime procrastination and any underlying stressors to help you sleep better.
